svg.text: Micro-Frontend Architecture — LLD
Composition Strategies
Build-time: npm packages — tight coupling, shared deps, no independent deploy
Server-side: edge/SSR stitching via ESI or Nginx includes — zero JS overhead
Client-side (Module Federation): runtime import() from remote URLs — most flexible
Module Federation: host exposes remoteEntry.js; remote declares exposes map
Shared singletons: React, ReactDOM in shared: {singleton: true, requiredVersion}
iframes: perfect isolation, hard to style, poor a11y, no shared routing
Web Components: custom elements as integration boundary — framework-agnostic
Single-SPA: lifecycle hooks (bootstrap/mount/unmount) per micro app
Routing, State & Communication
Shell router owns URL; micro-apps get path prefix — no full URL control
Cross-app events: CustomEvent on window — loose coupling, no shared store
Shared context: host provides auth/theme via window.__APP_CONFIG__ or props
State isolation: each micro-app owns its store — no shared Redux/Zustand
BroadcastChannel: cross-tab, cross-frame messaging for shared session state
postMessage: iframe ↔ host communication with origin validation
Contract testing: Pact/schema tests verify host↔remote interface stability
Avoid: shared mutable state across boundaries — causes tight coupling
Performance & Dependency Management
Dependency duplication: without sharing, React loaded N times — critical issue
Module Federation shared config: eager: false to avoid double-init on startup
Version negotiation: MF picks highest compatible version if ranges overlap
Lazy load micro-apps: import() on route change — not in shell bundle
Prefetch on hover: link rel=prefetch for next likely micro-app
Independent CI/CD: each micro-app deploys its remoteEntry.js to CDN
Cache busting: content-hash filenames; remoteEntry.js versioned separately
Fallback: if remote fails, shell renders error boundary + placeholder
Design System, A11y & Trade-offs
Shared design system: published as npm package imported by all micro-apps
CSS isolation: CSS Modules / Shadow DOM / BEM namespacing per micro-app
Global styles: CSS custom properties on :root from shell — shared tokens
Focus management: shell traps focus on route change; micro-app sets initial focus
ARIA landmarks: each micro-app declares its own region; shell wraps main
When to use MFE: 5+ teams, different deploy cadences, distinct domains
When NOT to use: small team, shared data model, same deploy cadence
Cost: operational complexity, duplicate infra, harder debugging across bundles
Module Federation: singleton React in shared config
Cross-app events via CustomEvent — loose coupling
Independent CI/CD: each team deploys remoteEntry.js
CSS isolation: Modules/Shadow DOM per micro-app
Use MFE only when 5+ teams, distinct deploy cadences
